notes: Overview: MassVec provides enterprise search+recommendation for retail and knowledge bases. Roadmap expects 200M->1B vectors over 12-18 months.
Key ask: deterministic latency at high scale and predictable unit economics. Current stack: FAISS CPU + bespoke sharding; struggling with p95 tail under heavy multi-tenant bursts.
AE intro (Liam): customer prefers Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput; Private for EU customers. Wants strong cost-per-query modelling.
SE summary (Nora):
- Target index sizes: pilot 200M vectors, production 500M-1B+.
- Embedding dims in prod: 1024 (text + multimodal concat), experimenting with 1536 for recency signals.
- Ingest pattern: continuous streaming updates (10k-80k vectors/day) + frequent bulk backfills (1.5M-3M batches).
- Query profile: mixed read-heavy; 30k QPS peak across geographies; session stickiness high for personalization.
- Latency objectives: ANN p95 <= 70-120ms for first-pass; end-to-end ANN+rerank p95 <= 220ms (target).
- Cost target: <= $0.006 combined (ANN + lightweight rerank) at scale; consider tiered pricing for cold shard queries.
- Rerank strategy: two-tier rerank: cheap distil model for most queries, larger BERT-family rerank for high-value queries. Want Redwood routing rules to select rerank tier.
- Index architecture preference: hybrid IVF-PQ + OPQ, with hot set fully in GPU memory, cold on NVMe; dynamic shard warming.
Security/compliance points:
- Must support SSO (SAML/OIDC), KMS integration, and per-tenant audit logs retained 36 months.
- Some customers will require air-gapped on-prem package for regulated lines of business.
POC state and observations:
- Hosted POC ran 15M vectors ingest: observed upload parallelism limits; Redwood suggested larger batching windows which increased throughput 3x with modest latency change.
- Comparative latency: Redwood quantized runtime outperformed MassVec's FAISS-CPU p95 under replayed arrival bursts by ~2x for 1k QPS test.
- Rerank path still a hotspot: GPU offload reduces p95 significantly but increases per-query cost; need Optimize recommendations for cost/perf sweet spot.
Customer quotes:
- 'We need a path to 1B vectors without linear cost growth. If Redwood can show unit economics and ops simplicity, we consolidate.'
- 'Failover behavior must be explicit: we cannot return stale results silently; prefer degraded-but-explicit fallback.'
Operational asks:
- Per-route and per-tenant cost & latency dashboards, caching recommendations for recurring queries, token-level billing visibility.
- Tooling to snapshot and shard-transfer with minimal impact; rollback to last known-good index in under 10 minutes desired.
Risks/concerns:
- Internal procurement favors multi-year committed Dedicated spend only if POC validates both cost and SLOs.
- Legal has additional redlines around export controls for embeddings derived from certain data types.
Next actions recorded:
- SE to produce 200M scaling runbook + synthetic traffic plan by 2026-03-09 (Nora).
- AE to align budget owners and lock stakeholder demo for infra execs (Liam).
- Optimize team to propose quantization + rerank cost model scenarios and recommended config (deliver by 2026-03-12).
